notes.meaning: David asks the Lord to bend down and hear his cry because he is helpless and in great distress. He does not point to his own worth, but brings his deep need before God. God's mercy is always drawn toward those who have nowhere else to look for rescue.

David asks God to protect his life because he is devoted to the Lord and innocent of the evil deeds his enemies accuse him of doing. Calling himself godly does not mean he thinks he is sinless, for he immediately places his faith in God alone. He looks to his heavenly Master to take care of a servant who trusts Him.

David asks for mercy, which is God's loving kindness to people who do not deserve it. He prays continually throughout the day rather than giving up. Believers can be sure that God hears when they make prayer a regular part of daily life.

David asks God to lift his heavy heart and fill it with true joy. He turns his inner feelings and thoughts entirely toward the Lord, knowing earth cannot satisfy him. When we seek close fellowship with God in prayer, He answers by giving us peace and gladness.

God is naturally good, ready to forgive sin right away, and richly generous in loving care to everyone who calls on Him. His mercy does not come from a tiny supply that might run out, but flows like an endless river. This unfailing goodness gives sinners great hope to come before Him without fear.

David asks the Lord again to listen to his earnest pleading. Repeating the request shows the deep feeling of a needy child rather than empty words. God gladly welcomes our prayers, even when our words feel clumsy and weak.

David resolves to pray whenever trouble strikes because he knows God actually responds. Calling out to the Lord is never a wasted effort or an empty exercise. When hard times arrive, turning straight to God brings real help and reassurance.

The idols of the surrounding nations cannot be compared to the living God in power, wisdom, or love. Those false gods cannot hear, speak, or do any wonderful deeds to help their followers. Only the Lord has performed mighty miracles and created the world around us.

Since God created all human beings, people from every nation will one day come and bow before Him in genuine worship. This points ahead to the good news of Christ spreading across the whole earth. In the end, all peoples will give honor to the one true Lord.

God is infinitely great and continually performs miracles and wonders in His creation. He has no equals and shares His throne with no one, for He is God all by Himself. Resting in His supreme power drives away our worries about earthly foes.

David asks the Lord to instruct him so that his everyday actions will follow God's truth. He also asks for an undivided heart, meaning a heart that is not torn between God and worldly desires. When God gathers our scattered desires into one focus, we are able to honor and obey Him with our whole life.

With a focused and single-minded heart, David promises to give thanks to God with all his strength. He wants to honor the Lord's name not just for a moment, but continually through life and forever. Sincere, wholehearted praise is the best gift a believer can bring before God.

David rejoices in God's immense covenant love because the Lord rescued him from the brink of the grave. The phrase depths of Sheol, or the lowest hell, refers to the deepest and most hopeless mortal danger imaginable. Remembering how God saved us in the past strengthens our confidence in His care today.

Proud and violent enemies have banded together to hunt down David and end his life. These men show total contempt for God, completely ignoring His law and presence. When people lose all reverence for God, they quickly treat other human beings with cruelty.

David turns away from his cruel enemies to praise the character of God. The Lord is full of tender sympathy, kind to the undeserving, patient when provoked, and always true to His promises. When life seems harsh, God's unchanging nature is our safest shelter.

David asks God to look toward him with compassion and fill him with divine strength. By calling himself the son of God's maidservant, he means he belongs to the Lord's household by birth, just like a child born into a master's family. Because he is God's rightful property, he can ask with confidence for his Master's protection.

David asks for a clear sign of God's favor so that his enemies will see it and feel ashamed of their attacks. When God steps in to help His servant, evil opponents are forced to realize they have been fighting against God Himself. Looking back at past answers to prayer reassures us that the Lord will provide comfort once again.
